churn_resistance.rationale: The architecture is upgrade-friendly: PokeAPI access, normalization and DTO typing are each confined to one module, and no framework internals or experimental APIs are relied on. It loses a point because the raw upstream boundary is `any`, a few presentation helpers are duplicated across the server/app layers, and there is no test or typecheck tooling to guard refactors.

findings.issue: The upstream PokeAPI boundary is untyped: `speciesWithPokemon` returns `{ species: any; pokemon: any }`, `TypeInfo.detail` is `any` (data.ts:39), and `fetchApi<T = any>` defaults to `any` (pokeapi.ts:24). The excellent DTO layer is only half a contract — tsc can't catch upstream shape drift.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the PokeAPI fields actually consumed (species, pokemon, type, move, ability) and type `fetchApi` call sites; keep them in `shared/types/` next to the DTOs.

findings.issue: `useRuntimeConfig()` is called inside a `computed()` getter (composable outside setup context), and the sprite URL pattern + media base are assembled in the client, duplicating knowledge the server layer owns for artwork.
findings.suggestion: Call `useRuntimeConfig()` at setup top level, or better: have the server DTOs emit the sprite URL alongside `artwork` so the client never constructs API URLs.

findings.issue: Client-side `s.types.map((t) => ({ name: t, label: typeLabels.get(t) ?? humanize(t) }))` re-implements the server's `typeRef()` helper (app/server/utils/data.ts:63), splitting label/humanization logic across layers.
findings.suggestion: Have `/api/species` return `TypeRef[]` per entry (it already has the labels server-side), so the client just renders.

findings.issue: error.vue duplicates the entire header/nav/footer shell from app.vue; any chrome change needs two edits.
findings.suggestion: Extract the shell into `app/layouts/default.vue` and wrap it with `<NuxtLayout>` in both app.vue and error.vue.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled TTL cache never evicts expired entries (only failed fetches are deleted), so the Map retains every unique URL for the process lifetime; it also can't be shared across instances.
findings.suggestion: Either sweep expired entries on set, or use Nitro's `defineCachedFunction`/`defineCachedHandler`, which provides TTL eviction and swappable storage.

findings.issue: Upstream fetches have no `AbortSignal`/timeout; a hung PokeAPI request holds the page render indefinitely (mapLimit caps fan-out at 32 but page-level fetches are uncapped).
findings.suggestion: Add `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` to `fetchApi` and surface the failure as a 502-style error.

findings.issue: No dev tooling at all: empty devDependencies, no `typecheck` or `test` script, so refactors of the sorting/filtering/spec-rule logic (MovesTable.vue:47, index.vue:23) are unprotected.
findings.suggestion: Add `vue-tsc`-based `typecheck` and a minimal vitest/@nuxt test-utils setup for the pure functions in `shared/utils/format.ts` and the sort logic.

findings.issue: `idFromUrl` parses IDs with a regex instead of the URL parser.
findings.suggestion: Use `new URL(url).pathname.split('/')` filtering — same length, more robust against trailing-slash/query variants.

findings.issue: HTTP status is set from a component via `useRequestEvent()`/`setResponseStatus` while the 404 itself originates in `createError` thrown deep in a server route — the responsibility is split across layers.
findings.suggestion: Let pages `throw createError({ statusCode: 404 })` on failed fetches so Nuxt's error pipeline renders error.vue with the status; or keep this but document it as deliberate.

summary: This is a genuinely current Nuxt 4 app: Nuxt 4.6, Vue 3.5, vue-router 5, `useId`, typed `#shared` DTOs, `compatibilityDate`, three dependencies total and no hand-rolled polyfills anywhere. Data access is confined to one thin server-side client plus a normalization module, so framework or upstream upgrades touch few files. The remaining churn risks are the untyped (`any`) upstream boundary, label logic duplicated between server and client, a copy-pasted error-page shell, and the absence of any typecheck/test tooling to guard refactors.
